title: Change entry failed
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/work-items/changes/failed, application/json, with which an adapter reports that it stopped trying to post the comment of a comment entry of the change feed (changes.schema.json) on its item, or to apply a change_request entry at its target. A report about a comment has comment_id, and a report about a change request has change_request_id and target; a report has one of the two, never both. A report about a change request may have detail; a report about a comment has none. For a comment, the control plane marks that comment not posted and stores reason, and keeps the comment with the item's other comments. For a change request, it stores reason, and detail when it is set, with the change request version, so the work item's pages show that the change was not made at that target. The adapter sends the report after a failure that trying again cannot fix. It also sends it with reason refused in two cases. One is an entry whose change_kind it did not list. The other is a change_request entry whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define. The detail starts with the fix, such as "Use an adapter that defines \"/target/extra\". The entry lists it in must_understand, and this adapter does not define it." The adapter makes the same report for a pointer below data that the artifact type of the change_kind does not define. For another kind of entry with such a pointer, it skips and acknowledges the entry (changes.schema.json). After a failure that trying again can fix, such as a timeout, a failed connection, a busy status or a 5xx status, it sends the report with reason unreachable, once its retries end. It sends one report for one comment entry, and none for a comment it posted. It sends one report for one change_request entry, and none for a change that it applied at the target. The control plane checks permissions first, in the order of refusal.schema.json: it returns 403 forbidden for a request the access key has no permission for. The request has no connection_id and no collection_ref, so connection_unknown, connection_ended, connection_suspended and collection_not_linked do not apply to it. The control plane returns a signed 204 and changes nothing for a comment_id that is not the comment_id of a comment entry in the adapter's change feed. It does the same for the comment_id of a comment that it already matched to a posted comment (source-item-comments.schema.json, comment_id), and for a change_request_id and target.collection that are not those of a change_request entry in the adapter's change feed, or whose entry the control plane already has a reply for (changes-submitted.schema.json). So a repeated or late report is never an error. On success the control plane returns a signed 204 with no body. The adapter acts on each answer as follows. On the signed 204, it does not send the report again. On 403 forbidden or 400 invalid_request, it stops sending the report. On a transient failure, no answer, a 5xx or an unsigned answer, it sends the report again, built anew as definitions.schema.json describes a retry, with backoff, and on a signed 429 it waits the seconds of Retry-After first. It stops sending the report once its retries of the report end, and logs the comment_id or the change_request_id. The adapter logs each refusal with the comment_id or the change_request_id, and never with the comment's or the change's text, an access key or a secret. The request is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. Set time from the adapter's clock and sign each request anew: the control plane returns an unsigned 401 for a time more than 300 seconds off its clock, either way, and for a request whose signature it has already seen; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. Send only the members of the revision that the control plane implements. The control plane ignores an undefined member of the body and of target, unless the must_understand of the body lists it.

version.description: The document format. Set it to 1: the control plane returns 400 invalid_request for any other version.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. Set it from the adapter's clock: the control plane returns an unsigned 401 for a time more than 300 seconds off its clock, either way.

comment_id.description: The comment_id of the comment entry whose comment the adapter stopped trying to post. Present exactly when change_request_id is absent.

change_request_id.description: The change_request_id of the change_request entry that the adapter stopped trying to apply. Present exactly when comment_id is absent, with target.

target.description: The target of the change_request entry, as the entry has it. Present exactly with change_request_id.

detail.description: The cause of the failure of a change request: one line of 1 to 1000 characters. Write first what to do about it, then the target's status and message, such as "Shorten the title, then try again. The target returned 422: title is too long." Optional with every reason of a change request. The adapter never puts an access token, a secret or a header in it. It has the character rule of a prose line (description.schema.json, $defs.line): no control character, so no line break, no U+2028 or U+2029, and no format character (category Cf) other than U+200C and U+200D. A report about a comment has no detail: the control plane returns 400 invalid_request for it.

reason.description: Why the adapter stopped. For a comment: item_gone, not_permitted, too_long or unreachable. For a change request: not_permitted, unreachable, target_gone, too_long or refused.

must_understand.description: The members of the document that the reader must understand, each as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) counted from the document, such as /reason. List each once, at most 32. A pointer has no line feed, and writes ~ only as ~0 or ~1. Each pointer is to a member that this schema defines. The control plane ignores a member that this schema does not define, unless must_understand lists it. It returns 400 invalid_request for a body whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define.

reason.description: Why the adapter stopped applying the change at the target: not_permitted, the target returned that the integration's account has no permission for the change; unreachable, each request to the target timed out, failed to connect, or returned a busy status or a 5xx status, until the adapter's retries ended; target_gone, the target returned that the place the change goes to does not exist, as after it was deleted; too_long, the title or the text is longer than the target's limit; refused, the target refused a request with a status that no other reason covers, such as 400, or 422 for a cause other than a missing place or a length limit, so the same request fails again, or the adapter cannot apply the entry, as for a change_kind that it did not list. The adapter writes the target's status and message in detail, with the fix first.

Why the adapter stopped trying to post the comment: item_gone, the source returned that the item does not exist, as after it was deleted; not_permitted, the source returned that the integration's account has no permission to comment on the item; too_long, the comment with its first line is longer than the source's limit for a comment; unreachable, each request to the source timed out, failed to connect or returned a busy status, until the adapter's retries ended.
